title: Tactical handoff pulsecards and postmortem access prototype
creator: Priya Shah
description: Brief summary: Build a compact, scannable 'pulsecard' UI element that surfaces incident-relevant micro-summaries in the Redwood Console timeline and on on-call handoff screens. Each pulsecard shows a 1-line incident summary, SLO delta, minimal cost delta (estimated token spend for the alert-run), and a single-click link to the postmortem and runbook anchors. The design explores two density modes (compact and expanded) and permission-aware controls (link visibility based on role). Goals: reduce handoff friction, speed postmortem access, and surface cost signals during triage. Scope: Console timeline + incident drawer + handoff modal + small responsive variants for tablet.
acceptance_criteria: Pulsecard component implemented in Console timeline with compact and expanded modes
Postmortem quicklink anchors open the customer postmortem in a new tab and record a click metric (telemetry event name: handoff.postmortem.open)
SLO delta and estimated cost delta appear inline and match mock data; values behind feature flag
Permission gating respects RBAC roles; designers confirm edge cases
Design reviewed and signed off by PM and Eng; usability test with 6 on-call engineers shows >80% task success for finding postmortem link
design_decisions: Use a 2-line compact pulsecard to keep density low in busy timelines
Show cost as a contextual micro-metric (rounded, with tooltip for breakdown) rather than full cost panel to avoid cognitive overload
Expandable details reveal a 4-item mini-footer: postmortem, runbook, primary contact, and last-deploy link
Prefer link-first CTA (Open postmortem) over inline secondary menu to reduce clicks
Use amber micro-badge for SLO deltas > 2% and red for > 5%; thresholds configurable in console settings
